requests.description: Creates a new connector profile associated with your Amazon Web Services account. There is a soft quota of 100 connector profiles per Amazon Web Services account. If you need more connector profiles than this quota allows, you can submit a request to the Amazon AppFlow team through the Amazon AppFlow support channel. In each connector profile that you create, you can provide the credentials and properties for only one connector.
requests.name: POST /create-connector-profile
requests.note: Replace {{AMAZON_APPFLOW_API_KEY}} with your API key | Set Content-Type to multipart/form-data for file uploads | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Enables your application to create a new flow using Amazon AppFlow. You must create a connector profile before calling this API. Please note that the Request Syntax below shows syntax for multiple destinations, however, you can only transfer data to one item in this list at a time. Amazon AppFlow does not currently support flows to multiple destinations at once.
requests.name: POST /create-flow
requests.note: Replace {{AMAZON_APPFLOW_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Enables you to delete an existing connector profile.
requests.name: POST /delete-connector-profile
requests.note: Replace {{AMAZON_APPFLOW_API_KEY}} with your API key | Set Content-Type to multipart/form-data for file uploads | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Enables your application to delete an existing flow. Before deleting the flow, Amazon AppFlow validates the request by checking the flow configuration and status. You can delete flows one at a time.
requests.name: POST /delete-flow
requests.note: Replace {{AMAZON_APPFLOW_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Describes the given custom connector registered in your Amazon Web Services account. This API can be used for custom connectors that are registered in your account and also for Amazon authored connectors.
requests.name: POST /describe-connector
requests.note: Replace {{AMAZON_APPFLOW_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Provides details regarding the entity used with the connector, with a description of the data model for each field in that entity.
requests.name: POST /describe-connector-entity
requests.note: Replace {{AMAZON_APPFLOW_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description:
Returns a list of connector-profile details matching the provided connector-profile names and connector-types. Both input lists are optional, and you can use them to filter the result.

If no names or connector-types are provided, returns all connector profiles in a paginated form. If there is no match, this operation returns an empty list.
requests.name: POST /describe-connector-profiles
requests.note: Replace {{AMAZON_APPFLOW_API_KEY}} with your API key | Set Content-Type to multipart/form-data for file uploads | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Describes the connectors vended by Amazon AppFlow for specified connector types. If you don't specify a connector type, this operation describes all connectors vended by Amazon AppFlow. If there are more connectors than can be returned in one page, the response contains a nextToken object, which can be be passed in to the next call to the DescribeConnectors API operation to retrieve the next page.
requests.name: POST /describe-connectors
requests.note: Replace {{AMAZON_APPFLOW_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Provides a description of the specified flow.
requests.name: POST /describe-flow
requests.note: Replace {{AMAZON_APPFLOW_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Fetches the execution history of the flow.
requests.name: POST /describe-flow-execution-records
requests.note: Replace {{AMAZON_APPFLOW_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Returns the list of available connector entities supported by Amazon AppFlow. For example, you can query Salesforce for Account and Opportunity entities, or query ServiceNow for the Incident entity.
requests.name: POST /list-connector-entities
requests.note: Replace {{AMAZON_APPFLOW_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Returns the list of all registered custom connectors in your Amazon Web Services account. This API lists only custom connectors registered in this account, not the Amazon Web Services authored connectors.
requests.name: POST /list-connectors
requests.note: Replace {{AMAZON_APPFLOW_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Activates an existing flow. For on-demand flows, this operation runs the flow immediately. For schedule and event-triggered flows, this operation activates the flow.
requests.name: POST /start-flow
requests.note: Replace {{AMAZON_APPFLOW_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Deactivates the existing flow. For on-demand flows, this operation returns an unsupportedOperationException error message. For schedule and event-triggered flows, this operation deactivates the flow.

requests.note: Replace {{AMAZON_APPFLOW_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values
